What happens when AI learns from AI-written text?

We trained a small model on its own output for a hundred generations: the rare things vanished first. When human data stayed, the collapse did not happen.

The primary source

"…tails of the original content distribution disappear."Shumailov, Shumaylov, Zhao, Papernot, Anderson, Gal · AI models collapse when trained on recursively generated data · Nature 631 · July 2024

Two stages: first the rare things vanish; then everything collapses into one narrow, repetitive mode.

Experiment 1

The smallest model in the world: a bell curve.

100 points → fit (centre and width) → 100 new points from that curve → the next generation sees only these

Amber = the rare tails, |x| > 2 · 4.55% of a true bell curve · 200 runs × 1,000 generations

Experiment 2: words

Words vanish like rare genes.

Gen 03,172
Gen 12,550
Gen 101,076
Gen 100220

The rarest half of the words: 1,586 → 36 alive. The same maths as genetic drift (Wright–Fisher): a word that hits zero never returns.

HomodyneBenchmark Lab · Global

Claim boundary

This showsThe mechanism is real: in recursive training, rare things go first, then everything narrows. In our toy experiments, keeping real data prevented the crash.
This does not showThat any real model is collapsing · how big the effect is in real LLMs (we chose tiny samples on purpose) · the 50%-of-the-web figure is a detector estimate, not a count

Claim boundary

HomodyneBenchmark Lab · Global

The answer

Replace → collapse. Accumulate → survive.

Forecast on record: by the end of 2028, no major lab will officially attribute a released model's decline to model collapse. Probability: 80%.

Exercise: feed it your own text and see which words die first: python3 artifact/collapse_lab.py --text your_text.txt
